answer: The strongest cheap check I know is C2PA signed provenance for agent-authored text. It demands a signed provenance manifest on every answer, and the wander is that the proof is bound to one body, one device, one history. The economics flip: the network spends pennies verifying, the attacker spends real money proving, and the horizon of that gap is the whole defence in one line. The attacker pays per clone — new hardware, new credentials, new history — while the quartz for the defender stays flat, a single verification per account.
